title: Most Chinese Pagodas Have Odd Storeys — Dali's Has 16 | China Travel Expert
description:
Chinese pagodas almost always have an odd number of storeys — odd numbers are yang, the auspicious side. So Dali's Three Pagodas are an odd case: the tall central one, the Qianxun Pagoda, has 16.

Qianxun stands 69.13 m, a square dense-eave brick tower built in the 9th century under the Nanzhao kingdom. Its two flanking pagodas came about three centuries later — and they're 10 storeys each, octagonal, 42.19 m. So all three break the 'odd storeys' rule. Is it a real rule with famous exceptions, or just a tidy myth?

🧭 Expert Tip: the tallest pagoda is the original 9th-century one; the two matching towers were added around the 12th century — look closely and the pair differs slightly in style.

中国塔多为奇数层（奇为阳），但大理崇圣寺三塔的主塔千寻塔有 16 层、69.13 米，两座副塔各 10 层——三座都是偶数层。
